metadata.research_goal: Create a backend-ready level-based basketball teaching draft from credible coaching, federation, youth-development, rules, and load-management sources. The draft defines beginner, intermediate, and advanced expectations, prerequisites, drills, avoid-until-ready gates, assessment signals, position-specific progressions, and level transition rules for core basketball skills, team tactics, and basketball strength and conditioning.

key_concepts.concept: Basketball skill is proven by transfer into live advantage, disadvantage, and equal-number situations.
key_concepts.details: Stationary technique is useful early, but level progression should depend on whether the player can execute while reading a defender, teammate, space, clock, score, and contact.

key_concepts.concept: Beginner basketball prioritizes legal movement, ball security, spacing, safe contact, and simple decisions.
key_concepts.details: Advanced actions such as ball screens, late-clock creation, switching schemes, and high-speed change-of-direction should wait until stops, pivots, passes, shot preparation, and defensive stance are repeatable.

key_concepts.concept: Every technical skill should progress from no pressure to guided pressure to live reads.
key_concepts.details: Coaches should add constraints gradually: weak hand, closeout, time limit, limited dribbles, help defender, shot clock, transition start, or scout-specific coverage.

key_concepts.concept: All players need a shared foundation before role specialization.
key_concepts.details: Guards, wings, and posts all need dribble-pass-shoot, defensive stance, rebounding, spacing, screening, and transition habits; specialization adds depth rather than replacing the common base.

key_concepts.concept: Basketball skill progression depends on movement quality under fatigue.
key_concepts.details: Jump volume, cutting volume, high-speed deceleration, contact, and tournament congestion should be managed because fatigue degrades landing, closeout, shooting mechanics, and decision quality.

technical_models.model: Catch ready, see the floor, threaten shot/pass/drive, then attack the highest-value advantage.
technical_models.level_notes: Beginner learns balance and eyes up; intermediate links catch preparation to one-dribble attacks and extra passes; advanced manipulates help defenders with pace, footwork, and deception.

technical_models.model: Legal stops and pivots are the bridge between movement, ball security, passing angles, and shot preparation.
technical_models.level_notes: Progress from jump stops and front pivots to stride stops, reverse pivots, pressure escapes, and contact-balanced gathers.

technical_models.model: Closeout, contain, angle, help, recover, block out, and secure the ball.
technical_models.level_notes: Do not separate closeout skill from the next action; the possession is not complete until the shot is contested legally and the rebound or outlet is secured.

technical_models.model: A pick-and-roll involves handler, screener, and the next defender, not only the two players in the action.
technical_models.level_notes: Beginner learns screen angle and wait; intermediate reads over/under/switch/help; advanced manipulates tag, low man, lift, short roll, and weak-side spacing.

tactical_rules.rule: Maintain useful spacing before demanding complex actions.
tactical_rules.teaching_use: In beginner and intermediate sessions, constrain players to corners, slots, wings, dunker area, or trail spots so driving lanes and passing windows are visible.

tactical_rules.rule: A paint touch should trigger a rim finish, kickout, dump-off, relocation, or offensive rebound responsibility.
tactical_rules.teaching_use: Assess whether players see help and punish rotations rather than driving into crowds.

tactical_rules.rule: Open rhythm shots from trained range are preferred over contested off-balance attempts.
tactical_rules.teaching_use: Unlock range, off-dribble threes, and contested finishing only after players show repeatable mechanics and decision quality.

tactical_rules.rule: The first three steps after a rebound, turnover, or shot attempt decide early advantage.
tactical_rules.teaching_use: Teach sprint lanes, outlet angles, rim run, ball-side fill, safety, and talk before adding complex secondary break options.

tactical_rules.rule: On defense, pressure the ball while all four off-ball defenders see ball and player, shrink space, then recover under control.
tactical_rules.teaching_use: Do not progress to switching, trapping, or rotation-heavy coverages until stance, closeout, help positioning, and rebounding are dependable.

physical_demands.demand: Basketball requires repeated short accelerations, hard decelerations, cuts, stops, pivots, and re-accelerations.
physical_demands.training_relevance: Teach braking mechanics, hip/knee/ankle alignment, single-leg control, and progressive change-of-direction volume.

physical_demands.demand: Shooting, rebounding, shot blocking, finishing, and closeout contests create repeated jump and landing exposure.
physical_demands.training_relevance: Monitor jump count, landing quality, fatigue, and contact tolerance before increasing plyometric or live-play volume.

physical_demands.demand: Screening, boxing out, driving, post play, and finishing require controlled physical contact.
physical_demands.training_relevance: Progress from body-position teaching and partner contact to live contact only when players keep balance, protect the ball, and respect legal cylinder principles.

physical_demands.demand: Players must process space, defender leverage, teammate movement, score, clock, and rules at speed.
physical_demands.training_relevance: Use small-sided games, constraints, and film feedback rather than only isolated repetitions.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Poor landing, valgus collapse, uncontrolled closeouts, and high-volume cutting increase lower-limb risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Hold progression when knee control, single-leg balance, deceleration posture, or soreness is poor; use strength, balance, and landing mechanics before higher intensity.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Year-round basketball, dense tournament schedules, and early specialization can increase overuse and burnout risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Protect weekly rest, planned time away from organized basketball, multi-sport or movement variety for youth, and honest fatigue reporting.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: High shooting volume, contact catches, deflections, and falls can stress wrists, fingers, elbows, and shoulders.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Build shooting volume gradually, monitor pain and mechanics, and delay high-volume long-range shooting until strength and form are stable.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Returning from ankle, knee, back, or concussion symptoms before game-speed tolerance can create re-injury risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Require medical clearance when relevant, pain-free sport-specific movement, progressive contact, and no next-day symptom escalation.

training_implications.implication: Use a blend of skill blocks, constraints, small-sided games, and short live segments.
training_implications.backend_use: Workout generators should avoid sessions that are only isolated drills once players pass beginner readiness.

training_implications.implication: Assess form, outcome, decision, and repeatability under fatigue.
training_implications.backend_use: Skill assessments should include technique signals, efficiency metrics, live-play decisions, and load response.

training_implications.implication: Youth progression is limited by maturity, training age, rest, and movement quality.
training_implications.backend_use: Youth athletes should trigger hold rules when training volume, pain, fatigue, or specialization risk is high even if skill metrics are strong.

Uses finger pads rather than palm slapping
Protects ball with body and off arm without pushing

position_specific_progression.posts: Use one-dribble power move and outlet dribble only after pivot control.

position_specific_progression.posts: Add face-up rip, one-dribble baseline/middle attacks.

skill_prerequisites: Can read help and second defender

Handle against traps and switches

assessment_signals: Creates paint touch or quality shot under live defense
Uses retreat and re-attack instead of panic pickup

position_specific_progression.guards: Primary handler, pick-and-roll manipulation, press control.
position_specific_progression.posts: Short-roll handle and dribble handoff keeper.

expectations: Shoot from close range with balance, guide hand discipline, eyes on target, and follow-through
Use layup footwork from both sides at low speed
Understand trained range
avoid_until_ready_gates: High-volume shooting with shoulder, wrist, or elbow pain

position_specific_progression.all: Use age-appropriate distance before role-specific shot diet.

expectations: Make catch-and-shoot attempts from trained spots
Prepare feet before catch

Use free throws as repeatability marker
avoid_until_ready_gates: Screens into shots before footwork is stable
assessment_signals: Maintains form across makes and misses
Makes open rhythm shots at useful percentage
Chooses pass or drive when shot is low quality

position_specific_progression.wings: Add corner, wing, lift, and drift threes when range is ready.
position_specific_progression.posts: Add short roll, trail, and pick-and-pop range only after close-touch efficiency.

expectations: Shoot from game range under closeout pressure
Use movement shooting, relocation, and quick decisions
Blend shot fake, one-dribble attack, and extra pass
Maintain mechanics late in practice

position_specific_progression.guards: Pull-up, step-back, and ball-screen threes behind decision gates.
position_specific_progression.wings: Movement threes, corner decisions, transition spacing.
position_specific_progression.posts: Pick-and-pop, trail three, elbow jumper, short-roll floater.

expectations: Make chest, bounce, and overhead passes to stationary and moving targets
Pivot to create passing window
Call names and meet the pass

Does not stare only at the ball

position_specific_progression.all: All positions learn chest, bounce, overhead, and safe outlet passing.

expectations: Deliver passes on time to cutters and shooters
Use pass fakes
Make simple drive-and-kick, post entry, and outlet passes
Understand spacing for passing angles
avoid_until_ready_gates: Advanced skip reads against rotating defense
assessment_signals: Uses fake and pivot to improve angle
Assist chances rise without turnover spike

position_specific_progression.wings: Extra pass, post feed, baseline drift pass.
position_specific_progression.posts: Kickout, high-low, and short-roll passing.

skill_prerequisites: Can pass with either hand in role actions
expectations: Manipulate defenders with eyes and timing

avoid_until_ready_gates: Primary playmaker load if turnover quality is poor or passes are late under pressure

position_specific_progression.posts: Hub passing from elbow, post, and short roll.

skill_prerequisites: Can dribble to basket under control
expectations: Make uncontested layups from both sides at appropriate speed
Use backboard

avoid_until_ready_gates: High-speed one-foot takeoffs if landing is poor

position_specific_progression.all: Every player learns both-side layups and jump-stop finishes.

expectations: Finish through light contact
Use inside-hand, outside-hand, power, and floater options
Read help defender and decide finish or pass

Can pass when rim protector commits

position_specific_progression.posts: Drop step, up-and-under, power finish.

expectations: Finish against length and rotation
Use deception, pace, body angle, and either hand

avoid_until_ready_gates: High-contact finishing volume when landing mechanics or soreness deteriorate

position_specific_progression.guards: Extension, floater, and craft against shot blockers.
position_specific_progression.wings: Power drives, bump balance, transition finishes.
position_specific_progression.posts: Seal, duck-in, short-roll, and offensive rebound finishes.

expectations: Use jump stop, stride stop, front pivot, reverse pivot, and basic defensive slides

position_specific_progression.all: All players learn ball pressure, gap, help, and closeout basics.

expectations: Read shot trajectory

position_specific_progression.guards: Manipulate defender with pace, reject, snake, and pass windows.

Basic ball handling, passing, shooting, finishing, closeout, and rebounding competence
Can participate in 1v1, 2v2, and 3v3 with spacing and safety
No unresolved pain or major fatigue response
Understands basic rules and safe contact

Cannot stop or land under control
Avoids weak hand completely
Needs constant coach direction to space or defend
Pain, soreness, or fatigue changes mechanics

required_evidence: Executes core skills under live pressure with acceptable efficiency
